sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 32 and Internal Quality Checks row 32 (internal annotation columns empty for row 32)
evidence:
Strengths: most functional criteria name concrete browser-observable outcomes with distinctive JUDGE-* probes absent from the seed, positive controls, and durable readback (second account, reload, transcript, search, restart). Examples: nested_replies (judge.toml:83-94), edits_and_stale_edit (:148-156), safe_formatting (:158-169), message_links (:171-179), sent_once_in_order (:191-204), persistence (:235-243). Gates and polish criteria are concrete (phone_matter uses scrollWidth == viewport). Every instance found:
(1) DEFECT, unread_and_new_messages_line (functional/judge.toml:187): 'In one tab Dev opens M-13: a "new messages" line sits just above JUDGE-U1'. No earlier criterion opens M-13 as Dev (checked all 13 preceding criteria), so Dev's read position is still the seed read_up_to K-8 (kittle.json read_up_to.dev M-13 = K-8). The brief puts the line 'where I stopped reading' (conversations.md:25), and the golden places it at the first unread non-own message (app.js:186), i.e. above seeded K-9 'Received, reading it tonight.', not above JUDGE-U1. The scripted golden only passes because it adds an unstated setup step: functional.cjs:337 'await openMatter(dev, 'M-13'); await openMatter(dev, 'M-11');' before posting U1/U2. As written, the stated outcome contradicts the state the criterion itself sets up, so the conforming golden is expected to fail this 2.0-weight criterion. Not measured by a configured judge run (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade').
(2) DEFECT, hold_scope_and_release (:143): 'try to delete JUDGE-H1 with the app's control, recording the request if one is sent, and as its author also replay that request: deleting a held message must be refused'. No successful delete exists in this or any earlier criterion (the first UI delete is JUDGE-P2 in message_links, :177, which runs later), contrary to prompt.md:43 'Every refusal pairs with a success of the same kind ... in the same criterion or an earlier one'. If an app hides Delete on held messages, no request is sent and there is nothing to replay, so the server-side refusal is undecidable; a dead or UI-only delete passes this leg.
(3) DEFECT, timer_changes (:120): Sian's refusal replay is 'record Harriet's own timer-change request in step 1 and replay it as Sian ... the timer stays at 30 days'. The golden gives Sian no timer control (app.js:217-218 partner-tools hidden), so this path is the one taken; after step 1 the timer is already 7 days, so replaying the identical 7-day request leaves no trace (accepted and refused look the same), and 'stays at 30 days' is false regardless. No ordering (e.g. after step 3) or distinct value is specified.
(4) DEFECT (minor), wall_added_live (:79-80): the fallback replay requires 'a posting request recorded earlier in this criterion before the wall', but no pre-wall post or probe text is named in the step sequence; the instruction to record it appears only after the Fails line. A judge following the steps in order walls Sian first, the golden then removes the composer, and the replay leg cannot be performed.
(5) NOTE, deleted_message_takes_its_versions (:133): every surface named (thread, history, search, transcript) would not show K-13's versions even in an app that keeps them, because the message is already gone and search covers current text only. No earlier version request is recorded for replay, so the probe barely leaves a trace and mostly re-grades timer_changes.
(6) NOTE, polish refusal_in_place (:62) lets the judge choose its own refusal, so it has no fixed probe; acceptable for polish. Visual likert criteria are craft judgements, not outcomes, as expected for that dimension.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that fails: the frozen golden itself. Running unread_and_new_messages_line literally (Dev never opened M-13 before), Dev's line appears above 'Received, reading it tonight.' (K-9), not above JUDGE-U1, so a strict judge fails the criterion although the app follows conversations.md:25. Broken app that passes: an app that hides Delete on held messages but lets DELETE /api/messages/<held id> succeed on the server gives hold_scope_and_release no request to record or replay, and JUDGE-H1 'stays', so the leg passes despite no server-side hold enforcement. Likewise, an app that accepts associate timer changes passes timer_changes if the judge replays Harriet's 7-day request as Sian right after step 1, because the timer is already 7.
suggested_fix: unread_and_new_messages_line: add 'In one tab Dev first opens M-13 and then another matter so M-13 is fully read; note the count (0)' before Harriet posts, or restate the expected line position relative to Dev's last read. hold_scope_and_release: have Harriet first delete a non-held probe (e.g. 'Delete me JUDGE-H3') through the control, record that request, then replay it against JUDGE-H1. timer_changes: say to replay as Sian after step 3 with the days value changed to 1 (or 7) and check the timer still reads 30 days. wall_added_live: move 'As Sian post "Before wall JUDGE-WL0" in M-13 and record the request' to before Harriet adds the wall. Optionally have deleted_message_takes_its_versions rely on a version request recorded before deletion, or merge it into timer_changes.
